author: AnthropicAI
text: In a two-layer attention-only model we find a more sophisticated algorithm we call an "induction head", which may explain part of in-context learning.  It searches for previous times a token occurred, and then looks one token forward to see what happened next: https://t.co/1h45MyShcD

author: AnthropicAI
text: We show that a one-layer attention-only transformer can be understood as a "skip-trigram model" and that the skip-trigrams can be extracted from model weights without running the model. https://t.co/wRyvONoxSL

author: AnthropicAI
text: We try to mechanistically understand some small, simplified transformers in detail, as a first step toward understanding large transformer language models.

author: AnthropicAI
text: Our first interpretability paper explores a mathematical framework for trying to reverse engineer transformer language models: A Mathematical Framework for Transformer Circuits: https://t.co/QFhQ8hB9jT

author: AnthropicAI
text: You can view this paper as a stepping stone - we've built the basic infrastructure and interface (pictured) for various alignment experiments, and will now be doing more ambitious research on top of this. More work in other areas to come! https://t.co/vsj7hhuz2b

author: AnthropicAI
text: We compare scaling trends for alignment from prompting, imitation learning, and preference modeling, and find ways to simplify these techniques and improve their sample efficiency. https://t.co/IOGnyubZlg

author: AnthropicAI
text: Our first AI alignment paper, focused on simple baselines and investigations: A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment https://t.co/jdO81KZA1A
